parsed.summary: An L-shaped kitchen run with upper lift-up cabinets and base units on wall 1, a tall storage and fridge column with a drawer bank and upper lift-up cabinets on wall 2, and an L-shaped worktop.

blocks.name: Wall 1 upper lift-up cabinets
blocks.contains: Three upward-opening wall fronts over the wall 1 worktop, with their hanging carcass.
blocks.reason: Three side-by-side fronts form one upper hanging run, which stays within the three-position limit. The hanging carcass is kept separate from the base run because it is a separate hanging unit. The shared carcass is an assumption based on the continuous upper line.

blocks.name: Wall 1 base cabinet run
blocks.contains: Two central base doors and one portrait door beside them, under the wall 1 worktop.
blocks.reason: The three base fronts form one continuous base run within the three-position limit. The portrait door is assumed to be part of the same carcass because it closes the same access opening; its operability is inferred.

blocks.name: Wall 2 tall storage pair
blocks.contains: Two full-height VEN-01 storage leaves at the left end of wall 2.
blocks.reason: Two tall leaves close one section and may not be grouped with a third tall leaf. The section boundary is inferred from the equal leaves and their vertical joints.

blocks.name: Wall 2 tall storage single
blocks.contains: One full-height VEN-01 storage leaf beside the storage pair.
blocks.reason: A third tall leaf cannot share a block with the pair under the tall-leaf limit, so it forms its own one-section column. Its carcass is assumed to be separate.

blocks.name: Wall 2 fridge column
blocks.contains: Two full-height leaves labelled as a fridge, forming an appliance column.
blocks.reason: Two tall leaves close one appliance section. Grouping them as one column follows the labelled appliance. Whether they belong to an integrated panel is an assumption.

blocks.name: Wall 2 base drawer bank
blocks.contains: Two columns of shallow drawer fronts stacked in two rows under the wall 2 worktop.
blocks.reason: The drawers share one horizontal base carcass across two positions, which is within the limit. Stacked drawers count as one position each.

blocks.name: Wall 2 upper lift-up cabinets
blocks.contains: Two upward-opening wall fronts over the wall 2 worktop.
blocks.reason: Two side-by-side fronts form one short upper hanging run. It is kept separate from the base drawers because it hangs separately.

uncertainties: The corner between wall 1 and wall 2 is not explicitly constructed; the corner carcass and how it joins the two base runs are not shown.
F06 may be a plinth or fixed panel rather than an operable door; it is kept in B02 pending confirmation.
The fridge leaves F10 and F11 may belong to an integrated appliance panel rather than a cabinet column.
The number of drawer fronts (F12–F15) is estimated; the lowest bands may be a plinth.
The worktop footprint is located from the top view p7-view-001 and may not match the elevations exactly.
